messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Hierarchical logistic regression model
parts:
Hi,

I think you want

m_inla_2 <- inla(outcome ~ -1 + treatment + f(patient, replicate = treatment, ...

Finn

On 16 Dec 2016, at 11:45, Lauri Lovén <lauri...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi!

I'm rather new to R-INLA, and asking for advice on a hierarchical model I'm fitting. My data looks as follows:

# A tibble: 8,819 × 3
   outcome treatment patient
     <dbl>    <fctr>   <int>
1        1         C       3
2        1         C       3
3        0         B       3
4        1         A       3
5        0         A       3
6        1         A       3
7        1         A       3
8        1         A       3
9        1         C       3
10       0         A       3
# ... with 8,809 more rows

Outcome is binary, treatment is is one of A, B or C, and patient is an integer identifier for each patient, running from 1 to 19. 

- - -

First, I'm fitting a logistic regression model, with a Gaussian individual effect for each patient. On glmer, I do it like this:

> m_mixed_1 <- glmer(outcome ~ -1 + treatment + (1 | patient), data = dat, family = binomial(link="logit"))
> fixef(m_mixed_1)
 treatmentA  treatmentB  treatmentC 
-0.08785882  0.01288948  0.81609816 

On INLA, I have

> m_inla_1 <- inla(outcome ~ -1 + treatment + f(patient, model = "iid"),
+                    data = dat, 
+                    family = "binomial", control.family = list(link = "logit"))
> m_inla_1$summary.fixed
                  mean        sd 0.025quant    0.5quant 0.975quant        mode          kld
treatmentA -0.08772447 0.1524914 -0.3903672 -0.08754480  0.2134063 -0.08717676 6.320478e-12
treatmentB  0.01292282 0.1515835 -0.2876114  0.01296702  0.3126568  0.01306768 7.391669e-12
treatmentC  0.81631416 0.1524544  0.5141136  0.81635840  1.1177119  0.81645531 6.411580e-12

As we can see, the MAP estimates agree with the MLE's of the frequentist model, as they should.

- - -

Next, I'd like to fit a model where the individual effect could be different (but still Gaussian) for each treatment:

> m_mixed_2 <- glmer(outcome ~ -1 + treatment + (1 | patient:treatment), data = dat, family = binomial(link="logit"))
> fixef(m_mixed_2)
 treatmentA  treatmentB  treatmentC 
-0.09976829 -0.07244137  0.83957396 

On INLA, I think this translates to

> m_inla_2 <- inla(outcome ~ -1 + treatment + f(patient, replicate = patient, model = "iid"),
+                  data = dat, 
+                  family = "binomial", control.family = list(link = "logit"),
+                  control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE))
> m_inla_2$summary.fixed
                  mean        sd 0.025quant    0.5quant 0.975quant        mode          kld
treatmentA -0.08772454 0.1524917 -0.3903676 -0.08754490  0.2134067 -0.08717689 6.312093e-12
treatmentB  0.01292283 0.1515839 -0.2876117  0.01296702  0.3126573  0.01306767 7.381971e-12
treatmentC  0.81631424 0.1524547  0.5141133  0.81635847  1.1177124  0.81645536 6.403190e-12

These, however, are somewhat different from the frequentist model results, and very close to those of m_inla_1.

Hence, my question: am I translating the m_mixed_2  model correctly into INLA syntax?

Thanks in advance,
Lauri
